subject: Textiles and Garment Construction
provisional_note: Semester 1 (Jul-Dec 2026) follows the official MoEST 2026 calendar. Semester 2 (Jan-May 2027) is inferred from the 2026 pattern and ends before the ACSEE examinations - replace it with the published 2026/2027 almanac before relying on those dates.

entries.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the properties of textile fibres, yarn and fabric
entries.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an understanding of the basic properties of fabrics used in cloth and garment construction
entries.learning_activity: (a) Perform different tests on fabrics (tensile strength, tear strength, pilling, colourfastness, dimensional stability)
teaching_learning_activities: Brainstorming: Guide the students to brainstorm the different methods of fabric tests
Exploration: Use online/ offline sources, guide the students to observe various methods of fabric tests
Practical work: Task the students to perform pilling and colourfastness tests
Study tour: Organise a study tour for the students to visit textile mills to observe the production of yarn and fabrics)
entries.assessment: Different tests on fabrics are performed clearly
entries.references: TIE, Textiles and Garment Construction for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Six: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the properties of textile fibres, yarn and fabric
entries.specific_competence: 1.2 Decorate fabrics for garment construction
entries.learning_activity: (a) Design and make household articles using embroidery, applique and quilt techniques
teaching_learning_activities: Plenary Discussion: Guide the students to conduct a plenary discussion on various decorative methods (embroidery, applique and quilt techniques) to design and make the household articles
Project Activity: assign each studens to design and produce household articles using decorative methods such as embroidery, applique and quilt techniques. Guide them to display their work for sharing
entries.assessment: Household articles using embroidery, applique and quilts techniques were well designed and made
entries.references: TIE, Textiles and Garment Construction for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Six: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the properties of textile fibres, yarn and fabric
entries.specific_competence: 1.3 Design and construct traditional clothing from selected ethnic groups in Tanzania
entries.learning_activity: (a) Design a potential Tanzanian national dress basing on traditional designs
teaching_learning_activities: Brainstorming: Guide the students to brainstorm the different types of traditional features that can be suitable for a national dress
